Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Bahá'u'lláh (author, Wikidata Q101054), died 1892; ʻAli Muhammad Shirazi Bab (author, Wikidata Q104273), died 1850; ʻAbdu'l-Bahá (author, Wikidata Q216954), died 1921. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Bahá'u'lláh, 1817-1892; Bab, ʻAli Muhammad Shirazi, 1819-1850; ʻAbdu'l-Bahá, 1844-1921") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: Bahá’í Prayers: A Selection of Prayers Revealed by Bahá’u’lláh, the Báb, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá, 1992, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/BahaiPrayers. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 96%, 100%, 100% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Bahá'u'lláh, ʻAbdu'l-Bahá, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
